---
title: "Descriptive Statistics"
subtitle: "Summarising, displaying and exploring data"
toc: false
---

How to summarise, display and explore data with one or two variables: frequency
tables and graphs, numerical summaries, association, the estimation of
distributions, robust summaries, inequality measures, data quality, index numbers
and the description of time series.

Each topic combines definitions and results with applications to data and
reproducible examples in **Python** ([Polars](https://docs.pola.rs/),
[NumPy](https://numpy.org/) and [Matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org/)). Exercises
include their solutions.

## Data

Most examples use real data: the microdata of the **Household Budget Survey**
(*Encuesta de Presupuestos Familiares*, EPF) of 2025, published by the Spanish
National Statistics Institute (INE). The survey records the characteristics,
income and expenditure of about 20,000 households living in Spain.

The data are downloaded and cleaned by two scripts,
`src/download/download_epf.py` and `src/processing/prepare_epf.py`, which produce
three tables in `data/processed/epf/`: households, their members and their
expenditure item by item. The variables are described in
`data/processed/epf/README.md`.
